name: Create rooms and beds schema with capacity rules
w: Beds are the unit that allocation, occupancy and fees all hang off. Getting the two-level room and bed model right now avoids a painful migration once real residents and invoices exist.
ac: rooms has hostel_id, floor, room_number, sharing_type, capacity, monthly_rent and status
beds has hostel_id, room_id, bed_label and status
capacity is constrained to a sane range and floor is indexed
Unique constraint on hostel_id plus room_number
Unique constraint on room_id plus bed_label
RLS is enabled on both tables using the hostel-scoped pattern
out: No separate room categories or amenity tables in the MVP.

name: Implement room creation form with sharing type and capacity
w: Owners configure inventory property by property. This form is the workhorse of setup, so it must validate hard on the server and still feel quick to fill in.
ac: Captures room number, floor, sharing type (single, double, triple, four plus), capacity and monthly rent
Server-side revalidation using the shared Zod schema
Success returns to the list with the new room visible
A validation failure preserves the entered values
Hostel id is taken from the session, never from the form payload

name: Auto-generate beds when a room is created
w: Manual bed entry is slow and error-prone, and a room whose beds do not match its stated capacity corrupts every occupancy number downstream.
ac: Creating a room with capacity N creates exactly N beds in one transaction
Bed labels are stable and predictable, for example 101-A through 101-D
A failure during generation leaves no room without beds
Re-running generation cannot create duplicate beds
Room capacity and bed count are asserted equal after creation
out: No custom bed naming patterns beyond the default scheme.

name: Prevent duplicate room numbers within the same hostel
w: Two rooms numbered 101 in one hostel make allocation ambiguous and will break any future room-level reporting.
ac: Database unique constraint exists, not just a UI check
Form shows a friendly error rather than a raw database error
The same room number in a different hostel is allowed
Leading and trailing whitespace and letter case are normalised
An integration test proves the constraint by attempting a duplicate insert
out: No soft-deleted duplicate handling beyond archive.

name: Implement bulk room generation for a floor range
w: A 60-room hostel is common and typing 60 rooms by hand is the single biggest reason owners abandon setup. Bulk generation is what makes onboarding realistic.
ac: Owner enters a number range, floor, capacity and rent
A preview shows exactly which rooms will be created before committing
Creation is all-or-nothing on conflict
50 rooms plus their beds are created in one action within a few seconds
Result screen reports how many rooms and beds were created
out: No spreadsheet or CSV import in the MVP.

name: Build room inventory list with filters
w: Owners need to see their inventory at a glance and find one room fast, especially on a phone while standing in the corridor.
ac: Table shows room number, floor, sharing type and occupied versus total beds
Filters by floor, sharing type and availability
Server-side pagination or virtualisation keeps a 500 bed hostel usable
Loading and empty states are implemented
Filter state lives in the URL so a view can be shared or reloaded
out: No drag-and-drop reordering and no graphical floor plan.

name: Implement room edit, archive and safe-delete rules
w: Deleting a room that has allocation history would silently destroy fee and occupancy history. Destructive actions must be blocked or converted into archives, never allowed to cascade.
ac: Editing rent and capacity is possible and reconciles bed count
Capacity reduction is blocked with a clear reason while beds are occupied
Rooms with allocation history are archived, never hard deleted
Archived rooms disappear from active lists but remain in history and reports
Every destructive attempt returns a specific, non-technical message
out: No bulk archive and no undo on archive in the MVP.

name: Implement bed status model and manual bed blocking
w: Beds go out of service for repairs, staff use, or because the owner is holding them. Without a blocked state those beds look vacant and get allocated by mistake.
ac: Bed status supports available, occupied, blocked and maintenance
A bed can be manually blocked or unblocked with an optional reason
A bed cannot be manually set to occupied; that state is derived from allocations
Blocked beds are excluded from vacancy counts
Status changes record actor and timestamp
out: No automatic maintenance scheduling or bed condition photos.
